Most of the oxygen we breathe today comes from marine photosynthesizers in the ocean, with estimates ranging from roughly half to about 70% of Earth’s atmospheric oxygen [d4,d5,d8]. Within that, phytoplankton and cyanobacteria are the dominant contributors, and the ocean’s upper 200 meters is the primary production zone [d4,d8]. Land-based sources such as trees contribute only about 28% of Earth’s oxygen, underscoring the ocean’s overwhelming role [d2,d6].
